principle: a credential surface is any value used to prove identity, not only columns named clave

surfaces.target: Auth0 username/password; Campus stores AUTH_SUB/state only
surfaces.migration: explicit per-account migration or reset; clear plaintext only after IdP identity is confirmed

surfaces.target: no password persisted during public enrollment; approved account uses managed IdP establishment flow
surfaces.migration: pending/unactivated records must not be copied in bulk; require establishment/reset when converted to managed identity

surfaces.risk: student code is a predictable/reused identifier treated as a password even though it is not named clave
surfaces.target: remove authentication meaning from CODIGO; preserve it only as academic/student identifier
surfaces.migration: legacy student must establish a managed password; once migrated, cédula+CODIGO fallback must never authenticate that account

surfaces.path: storage exposure confirmed; exact active authentication dependency must be verified before cleanup
surfaces.risk: readable password-like data remains at rest even if a different fallback currently authenticates
surfaces.target: no readable credential material in DATOS
surfaces.migration: inventory actual non-empty rows and references in QA/read-only analysis before deletion

surfaces.risk: must not be confused with a real identity migration path
surfaces.target: demo remains centrally read-only or isolated; no production-authority Auth0 identity
surfaces.migration: out of SEC-001 account migration; preserve SEC-004 boundary

closure_rules: no active USUARIOS account authenticates against readable clave
no prospect/free-user path authenticates against PROSPECTOS readable password
no student authenticates with NUM_CEDULA + CODIGO
DATOS CODIGO remains a non-secret identifier only
no readable password-like values remain in active credential stores
migrated accounts cannot fall back to any legacy credential surface
all legacy authentication branches have an explicit removal or expiry gate
demo authentication is evaluated separately under SEC-004
